title: Industrial Inspection Report for Concessional Import
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of the mandatory factory inspection report required for industrial entities to qualify for concessional import duties. Over time, the procedure has shifted from general committee-based verification to more specific administrative requirements, including the mandatory submission of the inspection report along with the Bill of Entry for each consignment.

evolution.procedure: Shifted from a one-time approval process to a continuous compliance requirement where the report-based approval must be attached to every import consignment.
evolution.institutional_oversight: Increased specificity in committee membership to include high-level customs policy officials.

timeline.change: Established the requirement for a committee (NBR, VAT official, Ministry of Industry) to inspect and submit a report (Appendix-1) for concessional import approval.
Refined the committee composition by explicitly naming the First Secretary (Customs Policy) as a member.
Introduced a procedural mandate requiring the certified copy of the inspection-based approval to be submitted with every Bill of Entry during customs clearance.

member_objects.resolved_text: ২। লিফট প্রস্তুতকারী শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক কারখানা স্থাপনের পর এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের অধীন রেয়াতি সুবিধায় কাঁচামাল বা যন্ত্রাংশ আমদানির অনুমোদনের জন্য চেয়ারম্যান, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড বরাবর আবেদন করিতে হইবে। উক্ত আবেদন বিবেচনার ক্ষেত্রে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড, সংশ্লিষ্ট ভ্যাট বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তা এবং শিল্প মন্ত্রণালয়ের প্রতিনিধির সমন্বয়ে গঠিত কমিটি আবেদনকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান সরেজমিনে পরিদর্শন ও যাচাইপূর্বক চেয়ারম্যান, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড বরাবর "পরিশিষ্ট-১" অনুযায়ী একটি প্রতিবেদন দাখিল করিবেন। উক্ত প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী প্রতিষ্ঠানের শিল্প স্থাপন সংক্রান্ত কার্যক্রম সন্তোষজনক বিবেচিত হইলে আবেদনকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানকে এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের অধীন রেয়াতি হারে পণ্য আমদানির অনুমোদন প্রদান করা হইবে। উক্ত অনুমোদন পত্রের সত্যায়িত ফটোকপি প্রতিটি পণ্যচালান খালাসের সময় বিল অফ এন্ট্রির সহিত দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

National Board of Revenue: The Chairman of the National Board of Revenue acts as the authority to receive applications from lift manufacturing industrial establishments seeking import duty concessions.

The National Board of Revenue is responsible for forming a committee, including representatives from the VAT office and the Ministry of Industries, to inspect and verify the manufacturing facilities of applicants before granting concessions.
Lift Manufacturing Industrial Establishm: These establishments must apply to the National Board of Revenue for approval to import raw materials or machinery under concessional duty rates following the establishment of their factory.
They are required to submit an approved authorization document along with their bill of entry for every consignment of goods cleared through customs.
Bill of Entry: A certified copy of the approval letter for concessional imports must be submitted along with the bill of entry during the customs clearance process for each shipment.
Concessional Duty: Eligibility for importing raw materials or components at concessional rates is contingent upon a satisfactory inspection report confirming the manufacturing capacity and operational status of the applicant.

National Board of Revenue: representatives from the Ministry of Industries
Bill of Entry: certified copy of the approval letter

সংশ্লিষ্ট ভ্যাট বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তার নাম ও স্বাক্ষর
তারিখ:

শিল্প মন্ত্রণালয়ের প্রতিনিধির নাম ও স্বাক্ষর
তারিখ:

জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের প্রতিনিধির নাম ও স্বাক্ষর
তারিখ:

National Board of Revenue: Washing machine manufacturers must apply to the Chairman of the National Board of Revenue to receive approval for concessional import of raw materials or components.
The National Board of Revenue oversees the committee-led physical inspection and verification process for applicant industrial facilities.
Upon a satisfactory inspection report, the National Board of Revenue grants the formal approval for the concessional import of goods.
Business Identification Number: Applicants are required to provide their Business Identification Number as part of the formal factory inspection documentation required to verify production eligibility.
Tax Identification Number: The Tax Identification Number is a mandatory disclosure in the factory inspection report to verify the credentials of the entity seeking concessional import benefits.
Bill of Entry: Manufacturers must submit a certified copy of their import approval letter along with the Bill of Entry during the customs clearance process for every shipment.
S.R.O. 125-AIN/2021: This notification establishes the regulatory framework for granting concessional duty benefits on the import of raw materials and components for local washing machine manufacturing.
The inspection committee utilizes the guidelines stipulated in this notification to evaluate the readiness of factories and recommend the extension of concessional import benefits.

National Board of Revenue: The committee formed under this order must submit a site inspection report regarding the applicant institution to the Chairman of the National Board of Revenue.
Concessional Duty: The institution is granted approval for importing goods at concessional rates provided their industrial establishment activities are found satisfactory according to the submitted inspection report.
Bill of Entry: An attested copy of the approval letter for the concessional imports must be submitted along with the Bill of Entry at the time of customs clearance for every consignment.

National Board of Revenue: Chairman of the National Board of Revenue
